rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and for the work you're doing on this. I'm not able to add my name (or Halcyon Threshold's) to the public signatory list this round — I have an employer disclosure process for outside AI-related activity that I need to complete first, and I don't want to get ahead of it. I'll keep an eye out for future letters once that's resolved. Thanks again, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: I declined (politely, leaving the door open) a press quote request from The Larkin Dispatch and a sign-on request from Corvid Institute's open letter.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for including Halcyon Threshold in the piece you're working on. I'm not able to go on record by name this week — I'm finishing an internal disclosure process at my day job before speaking publicly about this work, and I'd rather not get ahead of it. Sorry about the timing given your deadline. If it's useful for a future piece, I'd be glad to talk once that's settled. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: a press quote request from The Larkin Dispatch

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and glad the talk landed. Here's something concrete that would genuinely help: A landscape scan of independent AI safety evals — what's being measured right now vs. what's neglected. Sources to start from: Alignment Commons write-ups, Compute Commons grant summaries, and recent independent eval papers/benchmarks you can find. Deliverable: a simple spreadsheet with columns like: - Candidate eval/risk area - Who (if anyone) is already working on it - Rough compute/cost needed to do something useful there - Why it matters I'd love a first pass in the next couple of weeks if that's realistic for 5 hrs/week. This would directly shape what Halcyon Threshold works on next, so it's genuinely high-leverage. Happy to do a short call to calibrate scope before you dig in — let me know what works for you. Thanks again for offering your time. Morgan"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: given a concrete task — a landscape scan of what's neglected in independent AI safety evals, due back in ~2 weeks.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Great meeting you too. Thanks for the details — I'm scoping the specific project now (running a quick landscape scan so I can propose a concrete, neglected eval target rather than something vague) and plan to have the two-pager and budget to you before the 30th. One question for when I do: is there a preference for applicants with institutional backing, or are solo/independent applicants squarely in scope? Want to frame it right. Thanks, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Idris Bellamy (Emberfall): sent a holding reply — full 2-pager coming before Nov 30

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "halcyon-threshold-weekly-ops" (0 8 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Weekly schedule set up (Mondays 8am) so the operation keeps triaging inbox/grants/open items
